title: OSHA Fire Extinguisher Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1910.157)
subtitle: Use on the monthly extinguisher round and at the annual maintenance check.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A.
If an item fails, correct it or take the unit out of service; when a unit is removed for maintenance or recharging, provide alternate equivalent protection (1910.157(e)(5)).
Each item names the 1910.157 paragraph it is based on; read that paragraph when a result is unclear.

sections.title: Placement and access
items: Only approved extinguishers are in use.
Mounted, located and identified so it is readily accessible and reachable without risk of injury.
Unit is in its designated place.
No employee has more than 75 feet of travel to an extinguisher for Class A fires.
Travel from each Class B hazard area to an extinguisher is 50 feet or less.
Units for Class C hazards follow the Class A or Class B distribution pattern.
Class D agent within 75 feet of any area that generates combustible metal powders, flakes or shavings at least once every two weeks.
No carbon tetrachloride or chlorobromomethane extinguishers on site.

No soldered or riveted shell self-generating soda acid, self-generating foam or gas cartridge water units that are inverted to rupture a cartridge or start an uncontrollable pressure-generating chemical reaction.

sections.title: Monthly visual inspection
items: Visual inspection completed this month for each extinguisher and any hose used in place of Class A units.
Unit is fully charged and operable.

No new corrosion or mechanical injury. A unit showing it goes for hydrostatic testing unless a condition in 1910.157(f)(2)(i)–(v) applies, such as pitting corrosion, a soldered or welded repair, or fire damage; see the next item for units unfit for testing.
No shell, cylinder or cartridge that failed a hydrostatic test or is unfit for testing remains in the workplace.
Alternate equivalent protection is in place for every unit away for maintenance or recharging.

sections.title: Annual maintenance and hydrostatic testing
items: Annual maintenance check completed within the past year.
Annual maintenance date recorded and the record kept for one year after the last entry or the life of the shell, whichever is less.
Stored pressure dry chemical units needing a 12-year hydrostatic test emptied and maintained every 6 years (clock restarts at recharge or hydrostatic test); non-refillable disposable units exempt.
Last hydrostatic test falls inside the Table L-1 interval for the extinguisher type (5 or 12 years).
Carbon dioxide extinguishers and wheeled-unit nitrogen or CO2 cylinders tested within 5 years, or 10 years for nitrogen cylinders complying with 49 CFR 173.34(e)(15).
Hose ending in a shut-off nozzle tested on its extinguisher's interval.
Record shows test date, tester's signature and the unit's serial number or other identifier.
Tester is trained and uses suitable test equipment and facilities.

sections.title: Training
items: Program covering general principles of extinguisher use and incipient stage fire fighting hazards is in place.
Each employee received the education at hire and again in the last year.
Employees designated to use fire fighting equipment are trained on the equipment they would use.
Designated employees trained on initial assignment and no more than a year ago.
Where hose stations or standpipes replace Class A extinguishers, employees trained in their use during the past 12 months.

references: 29 CFR 1910.157: Portable fire extinguishers (Part 1910 Subpart L, Fire Protection)
